newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAYS TWO MORE MAY HAVE DEADLY EBOLA VIRUS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAYS TWO MORE MAY HAVE DEADLY EBOLA VIRUS.

text.p: South African health officials said on Wednesday doctors were monitoring two more people with symptoms possibly indicating the deadly Ebola virus.

"At present two contacts are being kept under close observation by Rietfontein Hospital because they have symptoms which might indicate Ebola," the Gauteng provincial health department said in a statement.
Cautioning that their conditions had not been confirmed, the health department added: "They have not been admitted, however, and their symptoms could well be unrelated to the Ebola virus."
A nurse became the first person to contract the disease inside the country last week.
Marilyn Lahana, a 46-year-old mother of two working in Johannesburg's upmarket Morningside Clinic, was diagnosed with Ebola after complaining of headaches and stomach pains.

Officials said she remained in a critical but stable condition in the Johannesburg Hospital, adding she had a secondary infection for which she was being treated with antibiotics, and was still on a ventilator.
Hospital Superintendent Trevor Frankish said any improvement in Lahana's condition would not be sudden: "Progress can only be measured in weeks, not in days."

While ruling out a public health threat from Ebola, health officials said they were monitoring anyone who could have come into contact with Lahana or the African visitor identified as the source -- mostly health and laboratory workers.
A total of 216 were being monitored, but the number under daily observation dropped to 36 by Wednesday as the incubation period expired for this group, the health department said.
Without early treatment, Ebola, which killed 245 people in Zaire last year and 35 people in two outbreaks in Gabon ealier this year, is fatal in 80 to 90 percent of cases.
With early diagnosis, the fatality rate can be lowered to around 30 percent, South African doctors said.
A doctor from Gabon, treated in the Morningside Clinic recently for fever and multiple organ dysfunction, is believed to be the source of the virus contracted by Lahana.
